userStories.title: Add archiveJournalOnMain core logic (pure move, atomic on-main commit)
userStories.description: As the cam orchestrator, I need a deterministic function that moves the oldest third of journal.md entries to scripts/cam/journal.archive.md on main when the entry count exceeds a threshold, so the journal stops growing without bound and no LLM summarization is involved.
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/commands/journal-archive.ts exports archiveJournalOnMain(options) with injectable cwd, spawnFn, threshold (default 50), and clock (now, default () => new Date()). [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts]

Entry counting considers only '## ' headers strictly AFTER the '<!-- ENTRIES_BELOW -->' marker; preamble headers (## Format, ## Guidelines, ## Entries) are never counted, moved, or altered. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts]

When entry count <= threshold the function returns a no-op success result ({ ok: true, archived: 0, entries: <n> }) and performs NO mutation: the fake spawnFn records no hash-object/write-tree/commit-tree/update-ref calls. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts]

When entry count > threshold the oldest floor(count/3) entries (minimum 1) are MOVED verbatim (byte-identical blocks, original chronological order) to scripts/cam/journal.archive.md: cumulative append after existing archive content read from main via git show; when the archive file is absent from main it is bootstrapped with a minimal header. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts]

journal.md is rewritten preserving the preamble and the ENTRIES_BELOW marker, with a pointer line referencing scripts/cam/journal.archive.md that carries the injected clock date, followed by the remaining (newest) entries. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts]

Both files land in ONE atomic on-main commit via commitTreeToMain with a 2-element FileWrite[] (commit message 'chore(cam): journal archive <k> entries'), followed by best-effort push; journal.md and journal.archive.md are read from main via git show, never from the working tree. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts]

Guard and push reuse the shared exports checkMainUpToDate and pushMainBestEffort imported from src/git/on-main.ts; no private copy is added. [oracle: grep -q "from '../git/on-main.ts'" src/commands/journal-archive.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file src/commands/journal-archive.ts + test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts (mirror the fake-SpawnFn pattern of test/commands/journal-append.test.ts). Reuse commitTreeToMain multi-file FileWrite[] support (CAM-90) from src/git/on-main.ts; import checkMainUpToDate/pushMainBestEffort from there too (jscpd duplication gate trips on a 5th verbatim guard copy, see the GOTCHA comment in src/git/on-main.ts lines 275-282). journal.ts already carries a private guard copy: do NOT copy it again. Result type follows the discriminated-union pattern of AppendJournalEntryOnMainResult (journal.ts). The live journal has ~112 entries after 3 preamble headers, so grep -c '^## ' over the whole file overcounts: the marker-relative scan is load-bearing. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard array index access. Do not add src/commands/journal-archive.ts to scripts/file-size-budget.json unless the gate demands it.

userStories.title: Wire cam journal archive [--threshold N] CLI subcommand
userStories.description: As a cam operator, I need 'cam journal archive' available as a sibling of 'cam journal append' so I can run the deterministic GC manually with an optional custom threshold.
acceptanceCriteria: parseJournalArgs accepts 'archive' as a subcommand and returns a new union member { mode: 'archive', threshold: number, help: false }; --threshold <n> parses a positive integer and an invalid or missing value after the flag produces a usage error and non-zero exit. [oracle: bun test]
dispatchJournal routes mode 'archive' WITHOUT reading stdin (append remains the only stdin path) and calls archiveJournalOnMain via an injectable dep so tests need no real git. [oracle: bun test]

On a successful archive run the command prints 'CAM_JOURNAL_ARCHIVED=<k> sha=<sha>' and exits 0; on the below-threshold no-op it prints 'CAM_JOURNAL_ARCHIVE=noop entries=<n> threshold=<t>' and exits 0; on failure it exits 1. [oracle: bun test]
JOURNAL_HELP usage and the top-level command list in index.ts mention 'journal archive [--threshold N]'. [oracle: grep -q 'journal archive' index.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: index.ts (parseJournalArgs ~line 1292, JournalDispatchDeps ~line 1307, dispatchJournal ~line 1357, JOURNAL_HELP ~line 345, command list ~line 95, case 'journal' ~line 2004) + test/commands/journal-append.test.ts or a new dispatch test file. GOTCHA: dispatchJournal currently reads stdin unconditionally before branching; archive mode must branch BEFORE the readStdin call or it hangs waiting for stdin. Sentinel parsing is a recurring bug class in this project (memory: supervisor-sentinel-parse-fragility): keep sentinel strings exact, single-line, machine-greppable. Keep exit-code semantics consistent with append (0 ok / 1 failure); do not reuse append's exit 3/4 codes.

userStories.title: Auto-invoke the archive check on the --cycle-close path
userStories.description: As the cam loop, I need the archive check to run automatically at cycle close so journal GC happens deterministically without operator or orchestrator discretion.
acceptanceCriteria: On the 'cam journal append --cycle-close' success path, the archive check (default threshold) runs strictly AFTER the CAM_JOURNAL_APPENDED write and recordCycleTokens, and strictly BEFORE the recycle marker is armed and CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE is emitted. [oracle: bun test with an injected call-order recorder]

The archive check is best-effort: an archiveFn that throws or returns ok:false logs a warning, does NOT change the exit code, and does NOT prevent marker arming or the CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE emission. [oracle: bun test]
Plain 'cam journal append' (without --cycle-close) never triggers the archive check. [oracle: bun test]
The archive check is injectable via JournalDispatchDeps so tests run hermetically without real git. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: index.ts (dispatchJournal --cycle-close block, lines ~1409-1448) + dispatch tests. Ordering rationale (load-bearing): once the recycle marker is armed the watcher SIGTERMs the orchestrator wrapper, which can kill this cam subprocess mid-archive; running the check before armMarker keeps the mutation window inside the safe part of the sequence. The existing sequence comment 'journal entry persisted -> cycle-tokens persisted -> THEN handoff' must be extended, not violated. The issue spec allows cycle-close OR boot check; cycle-close was chosen because it is the code-driven deterministic hook (boot-side check would add a second writer and a read on every boot).
